paper_title: Polynomial Bounds for the Graph Minor Structure Theorem
authors: Maximilian Gorsky (Discrete Mathematics Group, Institute for Basic Science (IBS), South Korea), Michal T. Seweryn (Computer Science Institute, Charles University, Czech Republic), Sebastian Wiederrecht (School of Computing, KAIST, South Korea)
statement: Conjecture 6.6: There exists a version of the LST with polynomial bounds and a number of major apices smaller than the least integer a such that H becomes planar after deleting a apex vertices. Regarding (iii), the proof by Kawarabayashi et al. [18] gives a good explicit 2t2 bound on the number of vortices. In this paper, we get a slightly better bound of 21 (t − 3)(t − 4) by showing that Kt is a minor of a graph which can be drawn in the plane with 21 (t − 3)(t − 4) pairs of edges crossing. Our proof suggests that the optimal bound is the minimum crossing number of a graph containing H as a minor. Here, the crossing number cr(H) of a graph H is the lowest number of edge crossings in a drawing of H on the plane. Let cr′ (H) denote the lowest value of cr(H ′ ) where H ′ ranges over all graphs containing H as a minor. Note that in general cr′ (H) can be much smaller than cr(H). For example, cr(Kt ) = Ω(t4 ) [83], whereas cr′ (Kt ) ≤ 12 (t − 3)(t − 4), as we have shown. We conjecture the following.

More precisely, we know that the excluded minor H does not embed in the surface Σ returned by the LST. This is optimal in the sense that for every surface Σ in which H does not embed, there exist H-minor-free graphs with meshes for which the LST requires either the surface Σ or a more complex one (obtained by adding handles and/or crosscaps to Σ). Furthermore, the surface-wall constructed by the proof ensures that for any graph H ′ embeddable in Σ, if the parameter k is sufficiently large, then H ′ is a minor of G. As for the apex vertices (ii), the situation is more complicated. The Flat Wall Theorem is known to hold with less than t − 4 apex vertices [20], [30], [31], which is an optimal bound (a grid with t − 5 apex vertices adjacent to each other and to the vertices of the grid contains no Kt -minor). In general, the currently known techniques give no hope for getting a bound on the number of apex vertices which is anywhere close to optimal, but we can bound the number of “bad” apex vertices. Let us call an apex vertex major if it is adjacent to a vertex which does not belong to any vortex. Dvořák and Thomas [80] showed that if the forbidden minor H becomes planar after deleting a vertices, then the LST is satisfied with less than a major apex vertices (if H = Kt , then a = t − 4). This variant has some interesting applications, including the recent proof of the Clustered Hadwiger Conjecture [81]. Wood [82] asked if the LST holds with polynomial bounds and less than a major apex vertices. A positive answer to this question would imply that Kt -minor-free graphs are (t − 1)-colourable with clusters of size polynomial in t. We suspect that our proof can be modified so that it has the property desired by Wood, although in such case the breadth of the Σ-decomposition would slightly increase. Proposition 6.8 (Bokal, Fijvaz, and Mohar [84]): Let t ≥ 9, then 1 1 ⌈ (t − 3)(t − 4)⌉ ≤ cr′ (Kt ) ≤ ⌊ (n − 5)2 ⌋ + 4. 4 2 For t ∈ [3, 8], we have cr′ (Kt ) = ⌈ 41 (t − 3)(t − 4)⌉. The authors of [84] believe that cr′ (Kt ) lies close to the upper bound given in Proposition 6.8. However, in order to prove the Conjecture 6.7, one does not necessarily need to find the exact value of cr′ (Kt ). It would for example be enough to show that there must always exist a minor model of H attaining crossing number cr′ (H) that is of polynomial size with respect to the order of H. Finally, the depth of the vortices. Thilikos and Wiederrecht [45] showed that the only obstruction to a vortex-free Σ-decomposition with bounded parameters is the presence of a “shallow vortex-grid” as a minor. There are several ways in which we can construct obstructions to a Σ-decomposition of small depth (see Figure 14), and it is not clear whether there exists a nice construction of graphs characterizing graphs admitting a Σ-decomposition of depth, say, at most 3. Our proof yields vortices of depth depending on the parameter k. Before we ask about a tight bound on the depth, we should ask if the depth can be bounded in terms of t alone. We believe that this is possible.
